statement_blocker: The catalog supplies no quantifier, deterministic-system model, phase or time space, invariant domain, regularity, definition of chaos, assumptions, or conclusion. It does not select Devaney chaos, sensitivity, entropy, Li-Yorke chaos, mixing, a horseshoe or symbolic factor, or a theorem about a named system. A universal reading is false for identity and constant dynamics, while an existential or definitional reading still requires proposition-changing choices.

bibliographic_discovery_candidates_not_c.citation: Gerald Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, American Mathematical Society, 2012, DOI 10.1090/gsm/140
bibliographic_discovery_candidates_not_c.candidate_locator: Section 11.3, preliminary-edition internal pages 295-297 (PDF pages 306-308), including the discussion of competing definitions, Devaney chaos, and Lemma 11.3; published-print pagination mapping remains open
bibliographic_discovery_candidates_not_c.candidate_summary: The text states that definitions of chaos differ, considers sensitivity plus transitivity, adopts Devaney chaos for continuous discrete maps on infinite metric spaces as transitivity plus dense periodic points, and derives sensitivity.
bibliographic_discovery_candidates_not_c.errata_boundary: The current errata uses printed-version pagination and says the matching printed-page-298 transitivity definition must quantify over nonempty open sets, W^s is corrected to W^+, and Problem 11.3 needs a no-isolated-points assumption; edition mapping, source admission, and independent review remain open.
